title: Subhanallah, thirty-three
hook: glory be to Allah, for what is beyond everything

segments.voice: Yesterday: adwamuha, even if it is little: the steady deeds are the most loved. Your line was small, steady, and back again. Today, one of the steadiest small things there is. Day one hundred fourteen.

A sunset over the water, and someone on the sand whispers: subhanallah. A baby's tiny hand closes around a finger: subhanallah. A crazy coincidence, a near-miss on the highway, a mountain out of a plane window. It's the word Muslims reach for when something is too big, too beautiful or too strange for ordinary words. And a hadith in Sahih Muslim sets it after every prayer, thirty-three times, counted out quietly.
screen: `A SUNSET, A BABY'S HAND.` → `TOO BIG FOR ORDINARY WORDS.` → `THIRTY-THREE, AFTER EVERY PRAYER.`

segments.voice: Subhanallah means glory be to Allah, and saying it is called tasbih. The root underneath, s-b-h, is the one the Qur'an uses for the sun and moon, each floating in its orbit. Some readers hear that picture inside the word: something moving far off, out of reach. The classical meaning is simpler and bigger: subhanallah declares God far above any flaw, any limit, anything a person could imagine. That's why it fits the sunset. The sunset is beautiful, and the One behind it is beyond even that. The Qur'an says, in Surah al-Isra, that the seven heavens and the earth and everything in them glorify Him, and there's nothing that doesn't hymn His praise, but people don't understand their glorifying. So in the tradition, the whole world is already saying subhanallah. The one praying is just joining in. After the prayer, there's a set. A hadith in Sahih Muslim says: whoever glorifies Allah thirty-three times after every prayer, and praises Him thirty-three times, and says Allahu akbar thirty-three times, and completes the hundred with there is no god but Allah alone, has their sins forgiven, even if they were like the foam on the sea. Tasbih is the first thirty-three. How do people count? A hadith in Tirmidhi tells the women to count on their fingertips, because the fingers will be asked, and made to speak; many use the joints of the right hand. A string of prayer beads is often called a tasbih, too, named after the word it counts.
screen: `A ROOT THE QUR'AN USES FOR ORBITS.` · `FAR ABOVE ANY FLAW.` · `THE HEAVENS ALREADY SAY IT.` · `THIRTY-THREE, THEN THIRTY-THREE.` · then, large: `THE BEADS ARE NAMED FOR THE WORD.`

segments.voice: Rest your right hand, palm up, and touch each joint with your thumb, one count each: fifteen joints is one pass, so go twice and add three. If you pray, say subhanallah softly on each count, not rushing; if not, say the word glory, or simply count, and on each count picture something beautiful you've seen this week. At thirty-three, let the hand rest.
Tasbih. Saying subhanallah, glory be to Allah, far above anything; thirty-three times after the prayer. Today's word.
Your line: glory. A sky, a face, a kindness: now there's a word for it. Day one hundred fourteen, counted.

howItsDone: After the obligatory prayers many Muslims say subhanallah thirty-three times, then alhamdulillah and Allahu akbar, counting on the fingers or on prayer beads, and they say subhanallah through the day at anything awe-inspiring.

they float, each in an orbit (21:33): the same root, s-b-h.

fork.setup: you've said subhanallah, alhamdulillah and Allahu akbar thirty-three times each after the prayer. that's ninety-nine. how does the hadith complete the hundred?
options: there is no god but Allah alone
fork.reveal: there is no god but Allah, alone, without partner, and the hadith promises sins forgiven even like the foam on the sea (Muslim).

original.note: Arabic: glory be to Allah, from the root s-b-h, which 21:33 uses for floating in orbit.

trapdoor: what you thought: subhanallah means wow.
what it means: glory be to Allah, declaring God far above any flaw or limit.
what a scholar hears: s-b-h, floating in orbit (21:33); 17:44, everything glorifies Him; and Muslim 597, the post-prayer hundred.

saying thank you to God for a blessing
a cheer shouted when your team wins
